text:
A fact-check reads the sentences a draft contains and asks whether a source supports them. It does not ask whether the sentences that should be there are there. TextOS's design record describes this failure plainly: a draft can be certified true while covering only one of the required points of its brief, an outcome it calls an empty draft certified true.

A short, two-sentence sample draft that TextOS once used in its tests is now kept as the reference case its brief check has to block. Such a draft can be accurate line by line and still leave the reader without the answer they came for. Keeping it as a test case means the gap between correct and complete is checked on purpose, not discovered by a disappointed reader.
